Label: C0.2 · T.E.S.C. Narrative
Summary: Construction stormwater narrative organized by the 13 required elements (clearing limits, construction access, flow rates, sediment controls, soil stabilization, slopes, drain inlets, channels and outlets, pollutants, dewatering, BMP maintenance, project management, low-impact-development BMPs) plus general notes on BMP installation, maintenance and removal (plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). Project description: total project area 0.45 ac, proposed impervious area 0.04 ac, area to be disturbed 0.30 ac, estimated cut 3,382 CY and fill 1,596 CY, stated as for the TESC narrative only and not for bidding or take-off (Item 15; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). The site is mostly flat, with grass turf along the north and south property lines and no trees or shrubs; runoff flows southeast to northwest into a ditch on the adjoining site along the north boundary; there are no streams, lakes, wetlands, residential or critical areas; soils are mapped as Roche-Killebrew complex, 2 to 10 percent slopes (Items 16–21; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). Sequence: install silt fence, construction entrance and inlet protection; remove pavement for sewer structures; clear and grade for the building addition and retaining wall; build them; install stormwater conveyance; pave and stabilize landscape areas (Item 22; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). Construction is expected from spring 2023 to fall 2024; no sediment ponds, diversions or waterways are used and no detention calculations are needed (Items 23–24; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual).

Label: C0.5 · Demolition Plan
Summary: Demolition plan with 25 keyed notes covering removal of existing pipe (40 LF 8-in and 60 LF 10-in effluent/outfall, 40 LF 4-in roof drain, 87 LF storm drain with a catch basin, 20 LF 6-in drain, 60 LF 1-1/2-in sump force main, 7 ft and 8 LF of storm drain, and the 8-in influent pipe), 149 LF and 119 LF of chain link fence, 61 LF of retaining wall, and the generator fuel tank with its concrete spill basin (Keyed Notes 1–2, 8–9, 11–12, 16–21, 24; plans_2Part-4 p.1, C0.5 — Verified-Visual). Removals follow their replacements: the effluent pipes come out after the interim 8-in HDPE pipe (C0.7) is installed and tested, the sump pump station and its piping after the new plant drain pump station, and the septic tank (SSMH 1285) after the new septic tank and influent pump station, with temporary pumps, piping and basins as needed (Keyed Notes 1, 3–5, 8, 11–12; plans_2Part-4 p.1, C0.5 — Verified-Visual). The Contractor keeps the 2-in water service and sump station power live until replacements are tested, protects the storm drain pump station manhole (DMH 1287), potholes storm, power and telecom before new work, relocates existing holding tanks on site per Owner, and sawcuts asphalt pavement (Keyed Notes 5–6, 10, 13–15, 25; plans_2Part-4 p.1, C0.5 — Verified-Visual). Construction phasing and the demolition schedule cover the existing basin: remove the 8-in slab over the original pre-aeration basin by saw cut near the building's east face, remove fill while supporting internal piping, bypass all flow during a time-critical step, complete a checklist (walls, coatings, penetrations, three weir gates) before accepting wastewater, and remove internal piping after the new flow splitter is operational (Construction Phasing 1–5, Demolition Schedule 1–3; plans_2Part-4 p.1, C0.5 — Verified-Visual).
